svg.title: Ranking-style history interaction for retrieval
svg.desc: Proposed three-path ExpertHistory. Latents select original events before the encoder, participate inside every full-history SASRec/HSTU block, and summarize all contextualized events. Item experts perform recent-event attention, selected-original-event attention, and activation-weighted full-history summary reads. No target ad enters user preparation.
svg.metadata: Proposed architecture, 2026-10-27. Sources: retrieval_model_improvement_plan.md and ../new_similarity_scoring_plan.md. Dimensions describe the design, not a verified implementation. No benchmark executed.
svg.text: Ranking-style history interaction for retrieval
PROPOSED REVISION · pre-block raw selection + latent-aware sequence blocks + full-history summaries
2 item experts · 512 latents / expert · up to 16 active latents / expert · 16 selected events / latent · recent R = 32 proposed
SHARED AD-DERIVED PARAMETERS · one canonical dictionary
Each item expert owns a dictionary; the same atoms connect ad queries to user-history processing.
Dashed purple arrows carry static model parameters. The current target ad is never an input to user preparation.
USER-ONLY PREPARATION · once per causal history prefix
ITEM-ONLY PREPARATION
INPUT · history IDs, valid-event mask, time / action payloads
Only events available at the scored prefix; retain original positions and repeated interactions.
Original event embeddings X · capture before any sequence block or dictionary adapter
Branch here: original-event memory bypasses the encoder; the entire sequence also enters the backbone.
Original-event K/V projections
Preserve pre-block event features.
Both direct-attention paths use these K/V.
Latent selection on original events
Each latent selects its top 16 valid events.
Selection reads original event embeddings.
Do not truncate the sequence encoder input.
Most recent original events
Keep the latest R valid events directly.
Independent of all latent selections.
Pack original events once
Recent + selected events share storage.
Keep original event IDs, positions, payloads.
Repeated item IDs remain separate events.
Shared storage does not merge the paths.
RAW BYPASS
The actual ad reads original event details.
Contextualized states never replace this memory.
REPEAT · full-history sequence blocks
Event → dictionary attention
Every event reads static ad prototypes.
All expert dictionaries participate.
Gated context changes the block input.
No target ad or future history is used.
SASRec / HSTU sequence block
Preserve causal masks and position / time.
All L valid events pass through every block.
Static dictionary K/V preserve causal dependencies.
Entire contextualized history H
One contextual state for every valid event.
Per-latent full-history summarization
Each latent reads the entire output sequence.
Normalize over all valid contextualized events.
Recent and selected events remain included.
PREPARED USER MEMORY · independent of every candidate ad
Original-event memory + recent list + all latent selection lists + all latent full-history summaries.
Prepare all 1,024 slots. Candidate activation is applied only when the scorer reads this memory.
Every event reaches contextualization and summarization; raw selections add a separate detail-preserving path.
INPUT · candidate item / ad IDs
Shared catalog or per-user candidate samples.
Shared item embedding / feature encoder
Cache item preparation for a fixed model version.
2 item experts → 2 distinct ad queries
Each expert keeps its own query through scoring.
Item-only gate supplies the final expert mixture.
Regular nonnegative sparse coding
Code each expert query with its own dictionary.
Keep up to 16 positive active atoms per expert.
Use continuous normalized activation weights.
Same active set can have different weights.
PREPARED ITEM STATE
Expert-specific queries and active atom indices.
Continuous coefficients and normalized weights.
Item-only expert gates.
Fixed-checkpoint catalog states can be cached.
Reuse item state across user requests.
No user history enters item preparation.
Recommendation and sparse coding train jointly.
COMPUTATION BOUNDARY
User side reads dictionaries as model parameters.
Actual ad queries and active supports enter scoring.
All expert dictionaries influence the shared backbone.
Each expert has its own selections and summaries.
Dictionary updates invalidate user and item caches.
This graph specifies the proposed revision.
USER–ITEM SCORING · three separate evidence paths per item expert
Route item state to prepared user memory · no history re-encoding
Actual query reads recent originals and the active-latent union; activation weights read contextual summaries.
1 · RECENT ORIGINAL EVENTS
Keep the latest R original events.
The actual expert query attends directly.
Separate recent-window normalization.
Preserves recent event details.
2 · LATENT-SELECTED ORIGINALS
Gather selected originals from active slots.
Deduplicate by original event position.
The actual expert query attends directly.
Retains relevant events from any history age.
3 · CONTEXTUAL SUMMARIES
Read full-history latent summaries.
Mix using continuous ad activation weights.
All valid events were included upstream.
Recent / selected events are not excluded.
Fuse three evidence vectors separately for each item expert
Small expert MLP reads all three vectors, query interactions, and presence masks.
The same event may supply original detail and contextual evidence; learned fusion combines them.
OUTPUT · item-gated mixture of expert logits
Use recommendation logits for next-item training or exact chunked catalog top-k.
Dimensions: B = users · A = 1 or B · T = padded prefix length · N = candidates · n = chunk size · P = packed original-event count.
R = 32 is proposed. Selected unions can cover all L ≤ 200 events at these budgets; reduced compute is not guaranteed. No benchmark run.
